claims.text: The initial material is as-cast or as-deposited HfZrTiTa0.53.
Deep cryogenic treatment is a suitable post-processing intervention for HfZrTiTa0.53.
The deep cryogenic treatment is performed in liquid nitrogen.
The deep cryogenic treatment uses a soaking time between 12 and 120 hours.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases lattice distortion in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases residual stress in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Increased lattice distortion reduces the difference between the movement rates of edge and screw dislocations.
Reducing the difference between edge- and screw-dislocation movement rates improves alloy plasticity.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the tensile ductility of HfZrTiTa0.53 relative to an untreated baseline.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the uniform elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53 relative to an untreated baseline.
Deep cryogenic treatment may increase the tensile strength of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The claimed improvement applies at room temperature.
The claimed improvement applies under tensile loading.
The applicable strain rate is 0.3 mm/min.
The falsification experiment tests temperatures from room temperature to 400 degrees Celsius.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement in tensile ductility and uniform elongation relative to untreated samples falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability is limited to room temperature, but the proposed falsification experiment extends through 400 degrees Celsius without specifying whether elevated-temperature results test the main claim or only its boundary.

The hypothesis calls 0.3 mm/min a strain rate, whereas the experiment and cited study specify a constant displacement speed. A true strain rate requires specimen gauge-length information and has units of inverse time.

Uniform elongation is a central predicted and falsifying outcome, but the measurement list specifies only generic elongation and does not explicitly require uniform elongation or the onset of necking.
